A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain all 25 pages, including readable text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–G. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports author-conducted OOD detection experiments, including adjacent OOD results in Section 5/Table 1 and additional adjacent and far OOD results in Appendix F/Tables 2–3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental outcomes in Section 5/Table 1 and Appendix F/Tables 2–3, including numerical comparisons across datasets and detection methods.

M1.justification: The Adjacent OOD construction and the described learning and OOD-scoring procedures are unchanged. No algorithmic component, architecture, objective, or inference procedure is introduced or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same facial-expression, Stanford Cars, Food 101, CIFAR10, and CIFAR100 data, with identical adjacent and far OOD coverage. The CC3M examples in Appendix G also remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within each experiment. Table 1 retains supervised MSP, SimCLR/RotLoss with KNN or SSD, diffusion LPIPS/MSE, and CLIPN CTW/ATD/MSP; Appendix F retains the same comparison methods.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 retain the same 75% ID/25% OOD class split, image preprocessing, ResNet50 configurations, training budgets, validation procedures, and AUROC/FPR95 metrics. Appendix F's evaluation settings are also unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 1's GradCAM failure case and Appendix G's examination of CLIPN pretraining examples are unchanged. No ablation, sensitivity test, robustness evaluation, or supplementary case analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report three experimental repetitions and different seeds for the class splits in Sections 5 and 5.2. Tables 1–3 retain identical plus/minus uncertainty reporting, with no new statistical procedures.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–3 and the reported qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1's supervised MSP Faces AUROC remains 70.8±0.3. No numerical correction, ranking change, or additional result appears.

T1.justification: The definitions, information-bottleneck equations, label-blindness results, and overlapping-OOD theorem are unchanged. Appendices B–D retain the same mathematical properties, assumptions, supporting lemmas, and complete proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: label-blindness theory, the Adjacent OOD benchmark, and empirical demonstrations of unlabeled OOD failure. Their scope and qualifications are unchanged.

C2.justification: Both versions give identical interpretations of label blindness, CLIPN's dependence on pretraining-label alignment, and stronger far OOD performance. Sections 4.4 and 7 retain the same theoretical boundaries and conditions under which unlabeled methods remain useful.

D1.justification: Implementation details, augmentation settings, training schedules, diffusion reconstruction settings, pretrained-weight descriptions, and the replication-code link are unchanged. No additional technical or code/data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The references and related-work discussion are identical. Section 3.2 retains the same distinctions from No Free Generalization and prior research on labels in OOD detection.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 20 Apr 2025 to v2 dated 6 Oct 2025. Manuscript wording, headings, section order, and appendix organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: All five figures and three tables retain identical content, captions, structure, and placement. Page organization is unchanged; minute text-position differences do not constitute a layout revision.

improvement.justification: The main text and appendices retain the same scientific arguments, proofs, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation. Changes to the arXiv stamp and PDF metadata do not resolve a paper-quality deficiency or introduce a meaningful deterioration.
